statement: Parchment radiocarbon interval alone establishes the date the visible Voynich text was written.
scope: Logical sufficiency of a support-material measurement; not a test of the actual inscription date
basis: Carbon dating measures the age of sampled parchment material, not the application of ink
test: Attempt inference from radiocarbon support to ink date without an independently dated writing event
result: The inference is invalid because storage and later inscription remain possible
caveat: This does not show the inscription was late.

statement: A digital canvas index may universally stand in for historical MS408 foliated-leaf identity without a mapping or exceptional cases.
scope: Universal identity assumption; NOT any particular Yale image-to-folio mapping or canvas count
basis: SRC-0006 directly records unnumbered leaves and inconsistently foliated foldouts
test: Search primary catalog for missing/unnumbered/ambiguously folded leaf numbering
result: Counterexamples documented; 1:1 unqualified index equivalence not warranted
caveat: A verified explicit canvas-to-physical-surface mapping may still be constructed; manifest not available

caveat: Other transcription variants may differ; missing full original-image inspection; a substring pchor in cheopchor is not the same exact EVA word. Does not refute general code or medical content EXP-0005: author publicly explains tokens may be parser-generated outputs; raw absence alone cannot falsify parser output.

statement: In the SHA256-frozen ZL3b-n v3b four-class EXP-0015 model, local suffix-class order is exchangeable within folios and within lines, conditional on their respective class compositions and line lengths.
scope: Five-fold held-out four-suffix-class representation and only the owner's exact version/ASCII IVTFF parser; NOT actual manuscript glyphs or semantic language

statement: The four-class EXP-0017 held-out Markov advantage is fully explained by exact position-dependent and line-length-dependent class frequency profiles within each IVTFF folio, without any additional within-line organization.
scope: SHA-256-frozen ZL3b-n v3b owner parser, folio 5-fold split; exact (folio, accepted-token line length, absolute token offset) composition-exchangeability null only
basis: EXP-0018 1000-permutation exact position/length controls per comma policy; 5-fold position-aware held-out comparison
test: Stratified token-shuffle preserving folio x length x position four-class marginals, score identical five-fold Markov-minus-unigram gain
result: All three strict nulls 0 of 1000 >= observed (empirical p=1/1001); all 3 looser folio-pos controls likewise. Secondary exploratory position-aware held-out plus prior-class classifier remains positive for all 3 policies.
caveat: Not a null preserving each line's own class counts; alternative line-specific compositions, scribal line templates or section effects remain. No semantic, language or cipher identification.

statement: The published VGM371/377 aggregate totals uniquely identify the 176 folio IDs and their tokenization from the source corpus.
scope: Inversion from totals alone under local SHA-frozen owner ZL3b-n v3b, P-line split policy; no claim about actual VGM356 source
basis: Two different integer-programming feasible 176-ID sets meet every published count but differ in 44 membership labels
test: Solve equality constraints on 176 folios, 3659 nonempty lines, 3633 lines>=2, 26 singleton lines, 30925 tokens and exact four-class totals; calculate CV model gain independently for two witnesses
result: Both local sets match all reported count totals exactly; Markov gains 0.0167126596 and 0.0165071738, not identical. Unique recovery from aggregate numbers impossible.
caveat: Does not falsify possibility that Franke applied a unique documented objective selection rule to his different VGM356 input. No evidence of intentional score optimization or misconduct.
